does: Bakes a pie of oiled phyllo sheets at a steady moderate heat until the layers dry out, turn golden and crackle, and the filling inside is set.

intro.what: Oiled phyllo layers bake into a crisp shell around a filling.
intro.why: A golden top can hide damp pastry underneath. Managing heat and escaping steam helps the whole layered crust become crisp.

how: Heat the oven before the pie goes in, and set the dish on a rack in the middle.
Brush the top once more with fat just before baking, so that it browns evenly.
Bake at a steady moderate heat. A fierce heat browns the top before the layers underneath have dried.
Turn the dish round if one side browns faster than the other.
Bake until the top is deep golden and the sides pull in a little. Leave the pie to settle before cutting, so that the filling firms and the layers stay crisp.

cues.text: The top is an even deep gold and the edges are dry and curled.
The pie crackles when the dish is moved, and the knife saws through a crisp top.

mistakes.mistake: Baking at a fierce heat, so that the top burns while the layers below are still pale and doughy.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat moderate and bake for longer.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting the pie straight from the oven, so that the filling runs and the layers go limp.
Covering the pie while it cools, which steams the crust soft.
mistakes.fix: Leave it uncovered on a rack.

quiz.question: Why use moderate heat for this layered pie?
choices: It keeps all the phyllo soft.
It gives the inner layers time to dry as the top colours.
It browns only the exposed edges.
quiz.because: Fierce heat can darken the surface before the layers underneath lose their moisture.

quiz.question: What should happen before slicing the baked pie?
choices: Cover it tightly to trap steam.
Slice immediately while the filling runs.
quiz.because: Settling helps the filling firm, while leaving it uncovered avoids steaming the crust soft.

quiz.question: Which sign suggests crisp phyllo layers?
choices: Dry golden edges and a crackling crust.
A pale top that bends silently.
Wet folds clinging to the dish.
quiz.because: Dry curled edges and crackling are texture clues for the pastry, rather than evidence about the filling.

quiz.question: The top darkens while lower layers stay doughy. What should change?
choices: Raise the heat to colour the top faster.
Use gentler heat and allow the layers to dry longer.
Cover the hot pie tightly after baking.
quiz.because: Gentler heat allows moisture to leave the lower layers before the top burns.

comes_after.why: The pie has to be layered and cut before it can be baked.

variant_of.differs: The food is sheets of dough brushed with fat, baked at a steady moderate heat until the layers dry and crackle around a moist filling, and rested before it is cut. A plain bake is for loaves and vegetables.
